subject.title: Feature Request: Cron Job Hooks System

question: Should OpenClaw core expose persisted per-cron lifecycle hooks that can run shell or webhook actions, and what trust boundary should own that behavior?
rationale: The remaining work changes public cron schema and can execute unattended local commands or network calls, which requires maintainer product and security intent rather than a mechanical fix.

options.title: Design a core hook API
options.body: Approve a narrow additive core cron hook/gate contract with permissions, cwd/env, timeouts, cancellation, output redaction, failure semantics, docs, and focused tests.

options.title: Route hooks outside core
options.body: Declare command cron plus plugin hooks as the supported boundary and track only missing plugin/API gaps separately.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Leave this issue open as an acknowledged product gap until maintainers are ready to own the cron hook trust model and public API.

recommendation.title: Design a core hook API
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow additive core cron hook/gate contract with permissions, cwd/env, timeouts, cancellation, output redaction, failure semantics, docs, and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest routing owner from current blame, prior issue review, and recent cron/protocol surface ownership.
